paragraphs: Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms "Janux Therapeutics," "Janux," "we," "us," "our" and similar references in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refer to Janux Therapeutics, Inc.

We are an innovative clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a broad pipeline of novel immunotherapies by applying our proprietary technologies to our Tumor Activated T Cell Engager (TRACTr), Tumor Activated Immunomodulator (TRACIr), and Adaptive Immune Response Modulator (ARM) platforms. The TRACTr platform produces T cell engagers (TCEs) with a tumor antigen-binding domain and a CD3 T cell binding domain, while the TRACIr platform produces bispecifics with a tumor antigen-binding domain and a costimulatory CD28 binding domain. The goal of our TRACTr and TRACIr platforms is to provide cancer patients with safe and effective therapeutics that direct and guide their immune system to eradicate tumors while minimizing safety concerns. Our initial focus is on developing a novel class of TRACTr therapeutics designed to target clinically validated TCE drug targets, while overcoming the liabilities associated with prior generations of TCEs. While TCE therapeutics have displayed potent anti-tumor activity in hematological cancers, developing TCEs to treat solid tumors has faced challenges due to the limitations of prior TCE technologies, namely (i) on-target healthy tissue immune activation that contributes to cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and healthy tissue toxicity and (ii) poor pharmacokinetics (PK) leading to short half-life.

Our first clinical candidate, JANX007, is a prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) TRACTr being investigated in a Phase 1 clinical trial in adult subjects with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). In December 2024, we announced updated interim clinical data for JANX007 demonstrating meaningful and prolonged prostate-specific antigen (PSA) reductions, evidence of anti-tumor activity, a favorable safety profile with CRS and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) primarily limited to cycle 1 and lower grades, and pharmacokinetics consistent with the TRACTr mechanism of action. In May 2025, we provided updated results from the patients reported in December 2024 that demonstrated consistent durability and safety profile supporting the initiation of Phase 1b expansion studies. In December 2025, we announced updated interim clinical data demonstrating durability across both once-weekly (QW) and every-two-week (Q2W) Phase 1a expansion cohorts. JANX007 continued to demonstrate a manageable safety profile, with CRS primarily limited to cycle 1 and grades 1 and 2, and preliminary Phase 1b data in taxane-naïve patients demonstrated rapid and deep PSA reductions with primarily grade 1 CRS. Based on the safety, pharmacokinetic and preliminary efficacy data observed to date, we initiated the first of our planned Phase 1b expansion cohorts designed to further characterize JANX007 and inform potential registrational development strategies. These cohorts are designed to evaluate JANX007 in clinically relevant patient populations, including taxane-naïve mCRPC, combination with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (darolutamide), and patients whose disease has progressed following prior PARP inhibitor therapy. In May 2025, we announced initiation of the Phase 1b expansion study in taxane-naïve mCRPC. These studies are designed to help refine dosing, patient selection and combination strategies and provide insights to support the design of future late-stage clinical development.

Our second clinical candidate, JANX008, is an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) TRACTr being investigated in a Phase 1 clinical trial for the treatment of multiple solid tumors. The first patient in this trial was dosed in April 2023, and in February 2024 we announced early clinical data demonstrating anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types, with low-grade CRS and predominantly low-grade treatment-related adverse events. In December 2025, we announced the initiation of Phase 1a expansion cohorts in selected solid tumor indications based on the efficacy and safety data observed in the completed dose-escalation portion of the study. Building on the results from dose escalation, the ongoing expansion cohorts are evaluating JANX008 in tumor types where early signals of activity and tolerability were observed. These studies are designed to refine patient selection, optimize dosing and inform the prioritization of indications for future clinical development.

Our ARM platform builds upon our expertise to redesign bispecific T cell engagers to address the limitations of conventional approaches in autoimmune diseases and oncology. The platform is designed to enable controlled T cell activation and expansion followed by contraction, with the goal of achieving deep and durable target cell depletion while improving safety and convenience. Based on nonclinical data, our lead CD19-ARM program has demonstrated rapid, deep and durable B-cell depletion in peripheral blood and lymphoid tissues with prolonged memory B-cell reset and a large safety window in non-human primates. We have initiated a Phase 1 clinical study of our CD19-ARM program (JANX011), which is designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of JANX011 in healthy volunteers. JANX011 is being developed for autoimmune diseases, and the initiation of this study represents an important step in the advancement of our ARM platform from preclinical development into the clinic.

We are also generating a number of additional TRACTr, TRACIr and ARM programs for potential future development, including a PSMA x CD28 TRACIr designed to enhance T cell activation and durability of JANX007 in patients with mCRPC.

TCEs are an emerging class of immunotherapies that bridge a tumor cell and a T cell to activate and redirect T cells to attack and eliminate tumors. TCEs have demonstrated promising anti-tumor activity in early clinical trials and in multiple animal models that rivals that of chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR T cell) therapies, with the distinct advantage that they are not cell therapies and have the potential to be offered as readily available, off-the-shelf therapies, which would avoid the lengthy, complicated, and expensive manufacturing process required for approved autologous CAR T cell therapies.
Three properties of existing TCEs have limited their potential to treat solid tumors:

• Cytokine release syndrome (CRS). CRS arises from the systemic activation of T cells and can result in life-threatening elevations in inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6 (IL-6). Severe and acute CRS leading to dose-limiting toxicities and deaths has been observed upon the dosing of TCEs developed using other platforms to treat cancer patients in prior clinical studies. This toxicity severely restricts the maximum blood levels of TCEs that can be safely dosed.

• On-target, healthy tissue toxicity. On-target, healthy tissue toxicity, arising from expression of the tumor target in healthy tissue and scarcity of highly tumor-selective antigens, is another limitation hindering the development of TCEs to treat solid tumor cancers. TCEs developed using other platforms not designed for tumor-specific activation have resulted in clinical holds and dose-limiting toxicities resulting from target expression in healthy tissues.

• Short half-lives. TCEs quickly reach sub-therapeutic levels after being administered as they are quickly eliminated from the body due to their short exposure half-lives. For this reason, TCEs such as blinatumomab (BLINCYTO) are typically administered by a low-dose, continuous infusion pump over a period of weeks to overcome the challenge of a short half-life and maintain therapeutic levels of the drug in the body. This continuous infusion dosing regimen represents a significant burden for patients.

We believe our proprietary TRACTr and TRACIr platforms offer the potential to expand the breadth of patients that can be treated with TCEs and non-TCE based immunomodulators while reducing the risk of life-threatening toxicities. Each of our proprietary TRACTrs and TRACIrs are comprised of an antigen-binding domain, a T cell-binding domain, domain-optimized peptide masks, an albumin-binding domain, and cleavable peptide linkers. The mask is a peptide designed to bind to the tumor or T cell-binding domain. It inhibits the binding domain's interaction with its target, thereby inhibiting the activation of T cells. The antigen and T cell-binding domains in our TRACTr and TRACIr product candidates may be covalently attached to peptide masks that block binding and activity until they are removed. We use proprietary peptide linker sequences composed of tumor protease recognition sites to attach these masks to the antigen-binding domains in a way designed to make the masks highly sensitive to removal by tumor proteases but highly stable in the absence of these proteases. In addition, we attach an albumin-binding domain to one mask, which is designed to extend the half-life of our TRACTr and TRACIr product candidates until they become activated inside a tumor.

While our TRACTr and TRACIr platforms are novel and unproven and our product candidates remain in the early clinical, preclinical or discovery stage, our technology is designed to offer the following features for the discovery and development of novel therapies for the treatment of solid tumors:

• Potential to reduce CRS and on-target, healthy tissue toxicity risk. By engineering our TRACTrs and TRACIrs with novel peptide masks that are designed (i) to be selectively activated in the tumor microenvironment and (ii) for any activated TCEs or non-TCE based immunomodulators to be rapidly cleared from healthy tissue upon escaping from the tumor, our product candidates have the potential to overcome the toxicity challenges of TCEs, non-TCE based immunomodulators and systemic immunotherapies in general.

paragraphs: We operate in a dynamic and rapidly changing environment that involves numerous risks and uncertainties. Certain factors may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations, and you should carefully consider them. Accordingly, in evaluating our business, we encourage you to consider the following discussion of risk factors, in its entirety, in addition to other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and our other public filings with the SEC. Other events that we do not currently anticipate or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our results of operations and financial condition.

We have a limited operating history, have incurred net losses since our inception, and anticipate that we will continue to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future. We may never generate any revenue or become profitable or, if we achieve profitability, may not be able to sustain it.

We are an early-stage biopharmaceutical company with a limited operating history that may make it difficult to evaluate the success of our business to date and to assess our future viability. Our operations to date have been limited to organizing and staffing our company, business planning, business development, raising capital, developing and optimizing our technology platform, identifying potential product candidates, undertaking research and preclinical studies for our lead programs, establishing and enhancing our intellectual property portfolio and providing general and administrative support for these operations. All of our product candidates and research programs other than JANX007 and JANX008 are in preclinical development, and none have been approved for commercial sale. We have never generated any revenue from product sales and have incurred net losses each year since we commenced operations. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, our net losses were $113.6 million and $69.0 million, respectively. We expect that it will be several years, if ever, before we have a product candidate ready for regulatory approval and commercialization. We expect to incur increasing levels of operating losses over the next several years and for the foreseeable future as we advance our product candidates through clinical development. Our prior losses, combined with expected future losses, have had and will continue to have an adverse effect on our stockholders' equity and working capital.

To become and remain profitable, we must develop and eventually commercialize a product or products with significant market potential. This will require us to be successful in a range of challenging activities, including completing preclinical studies and clinical trials of our product candidates, obtaining marketing approval for these product candidates, manufacturing, marketing and selling those products for which we may obtain marketing approval and satisfying any post-marketing requirements. We may never succeed in these activities and, even if we succeed in commercializing one or more of our product candidates, we may never generate revenue that is significant or large enough to achieve profitability. In addition, as a young business, we may encounter unforeseen expenses, difficulties, complications, delays and other known and unknown challenges. If we do achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain or increase profitability on a quarterly or annual basis and we will continue to incur substantial research and development and other expenditures to develop and market additional product candidates. Our failure to become and remain profitable would decrease the value of the company and could impair our ability to raise capital, maintain our research and development efforts, expand our business or continue our operations. A decline in the value of our company could also cause the loss of all or part of investments.

Since our inception, we have used substantial amounts of cash to fund our operations and expect our expenses to increase substantially during the next few years. The development of biopharmaceutical product candidates is capital intensive. As our product candidates enter and advance through preclinical studies and potential clinical trials, we will need substantial additional funds to expand our clinical, regulatory, quality and manufacturing capabilities. In addition, if we obtain marketing approval for any of our product candidates, we expect to incur significant commercialization expenses related to marketing, sales, manufacturing and distribution.

As of December 31, 2025, we had $966.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments. Based upon our current operating plan, we estimate that our existing cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments will be sufficient to fund our operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements for at least the next 12 months following the date of this Annual Report. We were incorporated in June 2017. To date, we have devoted substantially all of our resources to organizing and staffing our company, business planning, business development, raising capital, developing and optimizing our technology platform, identifying potential product candidates, undertaking research and development for our lead programs, establishing and enhancing our intellectual property portfolio and providing general and administrative support for these operations. All of our product candidates and research programs other than JANX007 and JANX008 are in preclinical development, and none have been approved for commercial sale. We have never generated any revenue from product sales and have incurred net losses each year since we commenced operations. We have funded our operations primarily with the net proceeds from the issuance of convertible promissory notes, the issuance of convertible preferred stock, the exercise of common stock options, proceeds from our initial public offering (IPO), the issuance of common stock and pre-funded common stock warrants in public and/or underwritten offerings and amounts received under a collaboration agreement with Merck.

We have incurred operating losses since our inception and have not yet generated any product revenue. Our net losses were $113.6 million and $69.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $351.4 million.

Our net losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year, depending on a variety of factors including the timing and scope of our clinical and preclinical studies and our expenditures on other research and development activities and the timing of any revenue recognition under our collaboration agreement with Merck. We expect our expenses and operating losses will increase substantially and that we will continue to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future as we conduct our ongoing and planned research and development activities and conduct preclinical studies and clinical trials, hire additional personnel, protect our intellectual property and incur additional costs associated with being a public company.

We do not expect to generate any revenues from product sales unless and until we successfully complete development and obtain regulatory approval for one or more product candidates, which will not be for many years, if ever. Accordingly, until such time as we can generate significant revenue from sales of our product candidates, if ever, we expect to finance our cash needs through equity offerings, debt financings or other capital sources, including potentially grants, collaborations, licenses or other similar arrangements. However, we may be unable to raise additional funds or enter into such other arrangements when needed on favorable terms or at all. Our failure to raise capital or enter into such other arrangements when needed would have a negative impact on our financial condition and could force us to delay, limit, reduce or terminate our product development or future commercialization efforts or grant rights to develop and market product candidates or to our platform technologies that we would otherwise prefer to develop and market ourselves. Based on our current operating plan, we believe that our existing cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, will be sufficient to meet our anticipated operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements through at least the next 12 months, following the date of this Annual Report.

In December 2020, we entered into a research collaboration and exclusive license agreement with Merck to develop TRACTr product candidates that are distinct from those in our internally developed pipeline (the Merck Agreement). Merck has the right to select up to two collaboration targets (each a Collaboration Target) related to next generation T cell engager immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer. Merck selected the first Collaboration Target upon execution of the agreement and selected the second Collaboration Target in May 2022. Merck received an exclusive worldwide license for each selected target and intellectual property from the collaboration. In return, we are eligible to receive up to $500.5 million per target in upfront and milestone payments, plus royalties on sales

of the products derived from the collaboration. Merck provided research funding under the collaboration through August 2024, after which our research services for both collaboration targets were completed.

Global economic and business activities continue to face widespread geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties, including those associated with public health crises, bank failures, inflation and monetary supply shifts, recent and changing tariff policy announcements, tariffs, trade tensions and retaliatory measures by other countries, supply chain disruptions, recession risks and potential disruptions from the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the war in the Middle East and related sanctions. Inflation generally affects us by increasing our salaries and fees paid to third-party contract service providers. We have considered potential impacts arising from the risks and uncertainties as described above and have not experienced any material disruption to our operations to date.

To date, we have not generated any revenues from the commercial sale of any products, and we do not expect to generate revenues from the commercial sale of any products for the foreseeable future, if ever. We recognized $10.0 million and $10.6 million of revenue under the Merck Agreement for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

To date, our research and development expenses have related primarily to direct and indirect expenses in connection with the development of our TRACTr, TRACIr and ARM platforms, discovery efforts and preclinical and clinical development of our product candidates. Research and development expenses are recognized as incurred and payments made prior to the receipt of goods or services to be used in research and development are capitalized until the goods or services are received.

我們是一家創新臨牀階段生物製藥公司，透過應用我們的專有技術於 Tumor Activated T Cell Engager (TRACTr)、Tumor Activated Immunomodulator (TRACIr) 以及 Adaptive Immune Response Modulator (ARM) 平台，開發廣泛的新型免疫治療藥物。TRACTr 平台產生具有腫瘤抗原結合域與 CD3 T 細胞結合域的 T 細胞活化器 (TCEs)，而 TRACIr 平台產生具有腫瘤抗原結合域與共刺激 CD28 結合域的雙特異性分子。我們的 TRACTr 與 TRACIr 平台目標是為癌症患者提供安全有效的治療藥物，以引導並引導其免疫系統消除腫瘤，同時降低安全性問題。我們的初步重點是開發一種新型的 TRACTr 治療藥物，用以針對已臨牀驗證的 TCE 藥物目標，同時克服先前世代 TCEs 的缺陷。雖然 TCE 治療藥物在血液腫瘤中顯示出強大的抗腫瘤活性，但開發用以治療實體腫瘤的 TCEs 面臨挑戰，原因是先前 TCE 技術的限制，即 (i) 靶向健康組織的免疫活化，導致細胞因子釋放症候羣 (CRS) 和健康組織毒性，以及 (ii) 藥物動力學 (PK) 不佳，導致半衰期短。

我們的第一個臨牀候選藥物 JANX007 是一種前列腺特異性膜抗原 (PSMA) TRACTr，正在進行一項針對成人晚期去勢抵抗性前列腺癌 (mCRPC) 病患的 Phase 1 臨牀試驗。2024 年 12 月，我們宣佈更新的臨牀數據顯示 JANX007 有顯著且持續的前列腺特異性抗原 (PSA) 減少，顯示出抗腫瘤活性，安全性良好，CRS 和治療相關不良事件 (TRAEs) 主要限於第一個治療週期且為低等級，藥動學與 TRACTr 作用機制一致。2025 年 5 月，我們提供更新的患者數據，顯示一致性耐受性和安全性，支持啟動 Phase 1b 擴展試驗。2025 年 12 月，我們宣佈更新的臨牀數據，顯示在每週一次 (QW) 和每兩週一次 (Q2W) 的 Phase 1a 擴展組別中，JANX007 有持續的療效和安全性。JANX007 繼續顯示出可管理的安全性，CRS 主要限於第一個治療週期且為一至二等級，初步 Phase 1b 資料在未接受過稅烷類藥物治療的病患中顯示出快速且深度的 PSA 減少，CRS 主要為一等級。基於目前觀察到的安全性、藥動學和初步療效資料，我們啟動了我們計畫中的第一個 Phase 1b 擴展組別，以進一步_characterize JANX007 並提供潛在登記開發策略的資訊。這些組別設計用以評估 JANX007 在臨牀相關病患羣中，包括未接受過稅烷類藥物治療的 mCRPC、與雄激素受體路徑抑制劑 (darolutamide) 組合，以及疾病在先前 PARP 抑製劑治療後進展的病患。2025 年 5 月，我們宣佈啟動針對未接受過稅烷類藥物治療的 mCRPC 的 Phase 1b 擴展試驗。這些試驗設計用以幫助優化劑量、病患篩選和組合策略，並提供資訊以支持未來晚期臨牀開發的設計。

我們的第二個臨牀候選藥物 JANX008 是一種表皮生長因子受體 (EGFR) TRACTr，正在進行一項針對多種實體腫瘤治療的 Phase 1 臨牀試驗。該試驗的第一位病患於 2023 年 4 月接受治療，2024 年 2 月我們宣佈早期臨牀資料顯示在多種腫瘤類型中均有抗腫瘤活性，CRS 為低等級，治療相關不良事件主要為低等級。2025 年 12 月，我們宣佈基於已完成劑量遞增部分的療效和安全性資料，啟動 Phase 1a 擴展組別，用以評估 JANX008 在選擇的實體腫瘤適應症中。基於劑量遞增的結果，持續進行的擴展組別正在評估在早期顯示出活性和耐受性的腫瘤類型。這些試驗設計用以優化病患篩選、劑量調整並提供未來臨牀開發適應症優先順序的資訊。

我們的 ARM 平台建立在我們的專業知識上，用以重新設計雙特異性 T 細胞活化器，以解決傳統方法在自身免疫疾病和腫瘤學中的限制。該平台設計用以實現受控的 T 細胞活化和擴增，隨後進行收縮，目標是實現深度且持續的目標細胞消除，同時提高安全性與便利性。根據非臨牀資料，我們的領先 CD19-ARM 程式已顯示在週邊血液和淋巴組織中快速、深度且持續的 B 細胞消除，並伴隨延長的記憶 B 細胞重置，以及在非人類靈長類動物中具有廣大的安全性範圍。我們已啟動針對我們 CD19-ARM 程式 (JANX011) 的 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，設計用以評估 JANX011 在健康志願者中的安全性、耐受性、藥動學和藥效學。JANX011 是為自身免疫疾病開發的，啟動此試驗代表我們 ARM 平台從非臨牀開發進入臨牀的重要一步。
我們也正在產生多個其他 TRACTr、TRACIr 和 ARM 程式，以供未來開發，包括一種 PSMA x CD28 TRACIr，設計用以增強 JANX007 在 mCRPC 病患中的 T 細胞活化和療效持續性。

TCEs 是一種新興的免疫治療藥物，用以橋接腫瘤細胞與 T 細胞，以活化並引導 T 細胞攻擊並消除腫瘤。TCEs 在早期臨牀試驗和多種動物模型中已顯示出強大的抗腫瘤活性，其效果與 chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR T cell) 治療相當，且其獨特優勢在於它們不是細胞治療，有潛力作為即用型、現成的治療藥物，這將避免已核准自體 CAR T cell 治療所需的長時間、複雜且昂貴的製造程序。
現有 TCEs 的三個特性限制了它們用於治療實體腫瘤的潛力：

• 免疫風暴（Cytokine release syndrome, CRS）。CRS 是由於 T 細胞的全身性活化所導致，可能造成致命性的炎症細胞激素（如 interleukin-6, IL-6）升高。在過去的臨牀研究中，使用其他平台開發的 TCEs（T cell engager）治療癌症患者時，曾觀察到嚴重且急性 CRS，導致劑量限制性毒性及死亡。這種毒性嚴重限制了 TCEs 在血液中安全劑量的上限。
• 靶向健康組織毒性（On-target, healthy tissue toxicity）。由於腫瘤標的在健康組織中也存在，且高選擇性腫瘤抗原稀少，因此導致靶向健康組織毒性，這是阻礙 TCEs 治療實體腫瘤癌症發展的另一個限制。使用其他非針對腫瘤特異性活化的平台開發的 TCEs，曾導致臨牀暫停及劑量限制性毒性，原因是標的在健康組織中表達。
• 短半衰期。TCEs 在給藥後會迅速達到治療濃度以下，因為其半衰期短，會迅速從體內清除。因此，如 blinatumomab（BLINCYTO）等 TCEs 通常會透過低劑量連續輸注泵在數週內給予，以克服短半衰期的挑戰並維持體內藥物的治療濃度。這種連續輸注給藥方式對患者來說是一項重大負擔。

我們認為我們專利的 TRACTr 和 TRACIr 平台有潛力擴展可使用 TCEs 和非 TCE 基礎免疫調節劑治療的患者範圍，同時降低致命性毒性的風險。我們專利的 TRACTr 和 TRACIr 均包含抗原結合域、T 細胞結合域、域優化肽掩蔽、白蛋白結合域及可切割肽連結器。該掩蔽是一段肽，設計用來結合腫瘤或 T 細胞結合域。它會抑制結合域與其目標的結合，從而抑制 T 細胞的活化。我們 TRACTr 和 TRACIr 產品候選藥物中的抗原和 T 細胞結合域可能與肽掩蔽共價結合，以阻斷結合和活性，直到這些掩蔽被去除。我們使用專利的肽連結器序列，由腫瘤蛋白酶識別位點組成，用以將這些掩蔽與抗原結合域連接，設計使其在腫瘤蛋白酶存在下高度敏感地被去除，但在無這些蛋白酶時高度穩定。此外，我們將白蛋白結合域連接到一個掩蔽上，設計用以延長我們 TRACTr 和 TRACIr 產品候選藥物的半衰期，直到它們在腫瘤內被活化。
雖然我們的 TRACTr 和 TRACIr 平台是新穎且尚未驗證，且我們的產品候選藥物仍處於早期臨牀、臨牀前或發現階段，但我們的技術設計用以提供以下特點，用於發現和開發用於治療實體腫瘤的新療法：
• 減少 CRS 和靶向健康組織毒性的潛力。透過工程設計我們的 TRACTr 和 TRACIr，使其具有新型肽掩蔽，設計（i）在腫瘤微環境中選擇性活化，以及（ii）任何活化的 TCEs 或非 TCE 基礎免疫調節劑在逃離腫瘤後能迅速從健康組織清除，我們的產品候選藥物有潛力克服 TCEs、非 TCE 基礎免疫調節劑及系統性免疫療法的毒性挑戰。

paragraphs: 你應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與我們財務報表及相關附註，包含於本年度報告表 10-K 中的「第 8 項 財務報表及補充資料」部分一併參考。下列討論包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。有關前瞻性陳述之完整討論，請參閱上文標題為「特別注意前瞻性陳述」之部分。我們實際結果可能與任何前瞻性陳述所表達或暗示者有重大差異，原因包括各種因素，包含於「第 1A 項 風險因素」標題下所列者。

此外，我們以下之討論與分析，重點為我們財務結果及流動性與資本資源，針對 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度之財務表現與狀況，包含這些年度之年對年財務表現與狀況之比較。針對 2023 年 12 月 31 日結算年度之討論與分析，以及 2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日結算年度之年對年財務表現與狀況之比較，請參閱包含於 2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度年度報告表 10-K 中，標題為「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」之部分，並於 2025 年 2 月 27 日提交至 SEC。

我們是一家創新臨牀階段生物製藥公司，透過應用我們專屬技術於 Tumor Activated T Cell Engager (TRACTr)、Tumor Activated Immunomodulator (TRACIr) 以及 Adaptive Immune Response Modulator (ARM) 平台，開發廣泛的新型免疫治療藥物。TRACTr 平台產生具有腫瘤抗原結合域與 CD3 T 細胞結合域之 T 細胞活化劑 (TCEs)，而 TRACIr 平台產生具有腫瘤抗原結合域與 costimulatory CD28 結合域之雙特異性分子。我們 TRACTr 與 TRACIr 平台之目標為提供癌症患者安全有效之治療，以引導並指導其免疫系統消除腫瘤，同時降低安全性問題。我們初期重點為開發新型 TRACTr 治療藥物，以針對已臨牀驗證之 TCE 藥物目標，同時克服先前世代 TCE 之缺點。雖然 TCE 治療藥物在血液腫瘤中已顯示強效抗腫瘤活性，但開發用以治療實體腫瘤之 TCE 仍面臨挑戰，原因在於先前 TCE 技術之限制，即 (i) 靶向健康組織之免疫活化，導致細胞因子釋放症候羣 (CRS) 及健康組織毒性，以及 (ii) 藥物動力學 (PK) 不佳，導致半衰期短。

pharmacokinetics (PK) 預期導致短半衰期。我們首個臨牀候選藥物 JANX007 是一種前列腺特異性膜抗原 (PSMA) TRACTr，正在進行成人晚期荷爾蒙抵抗性前列腺癌 (mCRPC) 病患之 Phase 1 臨牀試驗。我們第二個臨牀候選藥物 JANX008 是一種表皮生長因子受體 (EGFR) TRACTr，正在進行多種實體腫瘤治療之 Phase 1 臨牀試驗。ARM 平台建立於我們重設計雙特異性 T 細胞活化劑之專業知識，以解決傳統方法在自身免疫疾病及腫瘤學之限制。該平台設計為啟動並擴增 T 細胞，隨後收縮，目標為實現深度且持久之目標細胞消除，同時改善安全性與便利性。我們已啟動 CD19-ARM 程式 (JANX011) 之 Phase 1 臨牀研究，旨在評估 JANX011 在健康志願者中之安全性、耐受性、藥動學及藥效學。JANX011 開發用於自身免疫疾病，此研究之啟動代表我們 ARM 平台從臨牀前開發進入臨牀的重要步驟。我們同時正在產生數個其他 TRACTr、TRACIr 及 ARM 程式，以進行未來開發，包含一種 PSMA x CD28 TRACIr，設計用以增強 JANX007 在 mCRPC 病患中之 T 細胞活化與持續性。

我們於 2017 年 6 月成立。截至目前為止，我們已將幾乎所有資源投入於公司組織與人力配置、業務規劃、業務發展、籌資、技術平台之開發與優化、潛在產品候選藥物之識別、我們主要程式之研究與開發、智慧財產權組合之建立與強化，以及這些業務之一般及行政支援。除了 JANX007 與 JANX008 之外，我們所有產品候選藥物及研究計畫均處於臨牀前開發階段，且均未獲批准上市銷售。我們從未透過產品銷售產生任何收入，且自開始營運以來，每年均產生淨虧損。我們主要透過發行可轉換貸款、可轉換優先股、認購普通股選擇權、首次公開發行 (IPO) 所得、發行普通股及預資普通股選擇權、公開或經由經理人發行所得，以及與默克之合作協議所得資金，來資助營運。
我們自成立以來即產生營運虧損，且尚未產生任何產品收入。我們之淨虧損為 2025 年 12 月 31 日結算年度為 113.6 百萬美元，2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度為 69.0 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累積虧損為 351.4 百萬美元。
我們之淨虧損可能因季節與年度之不同而大幅波動，取決於多種因素，包括臨牀與臨牀前研究之時程與範圍、其他研究與開發活動之支出，以及我們與默克之合作協議下任何收入認列之時程。我們預期支出與營運虧損將大幅增加，且我們將持續在可預見之未來產生重大虧損，因我們進行持續且計畫中的研究與開發活動、臨牀前研究與臨牀試驗、聘僱更多人力、保護智慧財產權，以及因成為上市公司而產生之額外成本。

我們不預期在成功完成開發並獲得一個或多個產品候選藥物之監管批准之前，從產品銷售產生任何收入，而此過程可能需多年，甚至可能永遠無法實現。因此，除非我們能從產品候選藥物之銷售產生顯著收入，否則我們預期將透過股票發行、債務融資或其他資金來源，包括潛在之補助金、合作、授權或其他類似安排，來資金融資現金需求。然而，我們可能無法在需要時以有利條件或任何方式籌措額外資金或進入這些其他安排。我們若無法在需要時籌措資金或進入這些其他安排，將對我們之財務狀況產生負面影響，並可能迫使我們延遲、限制、減少或終止產品開發或未來商業化努力，或讓出開發與行銷產品候選藥物或我們之平台技術之權利，而這些我們較傾向自行開發與行銷。根據我們目前之營運計畫，我們認為現有之現金、現金等價物及短期投資，將足以應付我們預期之營運費用與資本支出需求，至少至本年度報告表之日期後之 12 個月。

2020年12月，本公司與默克公司簽訂研究合作及獨家授權協議，以開發與本公司內部開發管線不同的TRACTr產品候選品項（以下稱「默克協議」）。默克公司有權選擇最多兩個合作目標（各為一個合作目標），這些目標與下一代T細胞活化免疫治療藥物有關，用於癌症治療。默克公司在協議簽訂時已選擇第一個合作目標，並於2022年5月選擇第二個合作目標。默克公司對每個選擇的目標及合作產生的智慧財產權取得獨家全球授權。作為對價，本公司有權就每個目標收取最高達500.5百萬美元的預付款及里程碑付款，加上產品銷售後的版稅。
默克公司於合作期間提供研究經費至2024年8月，之後本公司對兩個合作目標的研究服務已全部完成。

全球總體經濟與商業活動持續面臨廣泛的國際政治與總體經濟不確定性，包括與公共衛生危機、銀行機構破產、通貨膨脹與貨幣供給變動相關的風險，以及近期及變動的關稅政策公告、關稅、貿易緊張關係與其他國家的報復措施、供應鏈中斷、經濟衰退風險，以及俄羅斯與烏克蘭衝突、中東戰爭及相關制裁等潛在影響。通貨膨脹通常會提高本公司支付給第三方合同服務供應商的薪資與費用。本公司已考量上述風險與不確定性可能產生的影響，截至目前為止，尚未經驗到對本公司營運造成重大幹擾的情況。
截至目前為止，本公司尚未自任何產品的商業銷售中產生任何收入，且在可預見的未來，本公司不預期會自任何產品的商業銷售中產生收入，若有的話。本公司於截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日止之會計年度，根據Merck契約認列收入為10.0 百萬美元及10.6 百萬美元。
截至目前為止，本公司之研究與開發費用主要與TRACTr、TRACIr及ARM平台之開發、發現努力及產品候選藥物之前期臨牀及臨牀開發相關。研究與開發費用於發生時認列，於取得商品或服務前所支付之金額則資本化，直至取得商品或服務為止。

與製造、商業化及依賴第三方相關之風險
paragraphs: 我們營運於一個動態且快速變化的環境中，涉及許多風險與不確定性。某些因素可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生重大不利影響，您應仔細考量這些因素。因此，在評估我們的業務時，我們鼓勵您一併考量以下風險因素的全部內容，以及本年度報告表10-K及我們其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）公開申報的資料。其他我們目前未預期或認為不重要的事件，也可能影響我們的營運結果與財務狀況。
我們的營運歷史有限，自成立以來已產生淨虧損，並預期未來一段時間內仍將持續產生重大虧損。我們可能永遠無法產生任何收入或實現盈利，或即使實現盈利，也可能無法維持。

我們是一家早期階段的生物科技製藥公司，營運歷史有限，這可能使評估我們業務的成效及未來可持續性變得困難。截至目前為止，我們的營運活動僅限於組織與僱用員工、業務規劃、業務發展、籌資、開發與優化我們的技術平台、識別潛在產品候選物、進行我們主要計畫的臨牀前研究、建立與強化我們的智慧財產權組合，以及提供這些營運活動的一般及行政支援。我們所有產品候選物與研究計畫，除了JANX007與JANX008外，皆處於臨牀前開發階段，且無任何產品已獲得商業銷售許可。我們從未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，且自開始營運以來，每年皆產生淨虧損。截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日，我們的淨虧損分別為113.6 百萬美元與69.0 百萬美元。我們預期，若能實現的話，將需數年時間才能使產品候選物準備好進行監管審批與商業化。我們預期在未來數年內，營運虧損將持續增加，且在可預見的未來內皆如此。我們過去的虧損，加上預期未來的虧損，已對股東權益與營運資金產生並持續產生負面影響。

要成為並維持盈利，我們必須開發並最終商業化具有重大市場潛力的產品或產品組合。這將需要我們成功完成產品候選物的臨牀前研究與臨牀試驗、取得這些產品候選物的市場許可、製造、行銷與銷售這些產品（若我們取得市場許可），並符合任何上市後的相關要求。我們可能永遠無法成功完成這些活動，即使我們成功商業化一個或數個產品候選物，也可能永遠無法產生足夠的收入以實現盈利。此外，作為一家年輕企業，我們可能面臨預期之外的費用、困難、複雜問題、延誤及其他已知與未知的挑戰。即使我們實現盈利，也可能無法維持或提高季度或年度的盈利，且我們將持續產生大量研究與開發及其他費用，以開發與行銷更多產品候選物。我們若無法成為並維持盈利，將降低公司的價值，並可能影響我們籌資能力、維持研究與開發工作、擴展業務或持續營運。公司價值的下降也可能導致投資者蒙受全部或部分損失。
自成立以來，我們已使用大量現金以支應營運費用，並預期未來幾年內營運費用將大幅增加。生物科技製藥產品候選物的開發屬於高成本性質。當我們的產品候選物進入並進展至臨牀前研究與潛在臨牀試驗階段時，我們將需要大量額外資金以擴展臨牀、監管、品質與製造能力。此外，若我們取得任何產品候選物的市場許可，我們預期將產生與行銷、銷售、製造與分銷相關的重大商業化費用。
